'''Paolo Aluffi''' is an Italian-American [[mathematician]] specializing in [[algebraic geometry]] who is known for his book ''[[Algebra: Chapter 0]]''. His research primarily focuses on [[characteristic class]]es. Throughout his career Aluffi has received funding from the [[Simons Foundation]], the [[National Security Agency]], and the [[National Science Foundation]]. He is currently a distinguished research professor at [[Florida State University]] and serves as one of the managing editors for the [[Journal of Singularities]].<ref name="vita" >{{cite web |title=Paolo Aluffi |url=https://www.math.fsu.edu/~aluffi/ps+pdfs/NewCV.pdf |access-date=5 August 2025 |archive-date=17 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250217143651/https://www.math.fsu.edu/~aluffi/ps+pdfs/NewCV.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Education==
In 1983, Aluffi received his [[laurea]] in mathematics from the [[University of Turin]] in Italy, mentored by [[Alberto Collino]]. Four years later he completed his Ph.D. at [[Brown University]].<ref name="vita" /> His dissertation, ''On Some Characteristic Numbers for Smooth Plane Curves'', was written under the supervision of [[William Fulton (mathematician)|William Fulton]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy | 4479 | Paolo Aluffi}}</ref>

==Career==
With the completion of his Ph.D. in 1987, Aluffi spent two years as a Dickson Instructor at the [[University of Chicago]] followed by another two years as a visiting assistant professor at [[Oklahoma State University]]. He moved to [[Florida State University]] as an assistant professor in 1991 where he became a full professor by 2000.<ref>{{ORCID|0000-0002-8249-685X}}</ref> Since 2009 he has also held a visiting position at [[Caltech]].<ref name="vita" >{{cite web |title=Paolo Aluffi |url=https://www.math.fsu.edu/~aluffi/ps+pdfs/NewCV.pdf |access-date=5 August 2025 |archive-date=17 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250217143651/https://www.math.fsu.edu/~aluffi/ps+pdfs/NewCV.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Caltech homepage" >{{cite web |title=Paolo Aluffi's webpage at Caltech |url=https://www.pma.caltech.edu/people/paolo-aluffi}}</ref>
In 2024 he was named a Distinguished Research Professor at Florida State University.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Haughney |first1=Kathleen |title=FSU names four faculty distinguished research professor |url=https://news.fsu.edu/news/university-news/2024/04/25/fsu-names-four-faculty-distinguished-research-professor/ |website=Florida State University News |access-date=5 August 2025 |date=25 April 2024 |archive-date=14 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250514173600/https://news.fsu.edu/news/university-news/2024/04/25/fsu-names-four-faculty-distinguished-research-professor/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

At Florida State University Aluffi wrote ''[[Algebra: Chapter 0]]'', a graduate-level [[abstract algebra]] textbook published by the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Aluffi |first1=Paolo |title=Algebra: Chapter 0 |url=https://www.ams.org/books/gsm/104/ |website=American Mathematical Society |access-date=16 August 2025 |language=en |date=15 July 2009}}</ref> The book is an edited compilation of transcripts from his [[abstract algebra]] lectures.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Aluffi |first1=Paolo |title=Algebra: Chapter 0 |date=2009 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |location=Providence (R.I.) |isbn=978-0-8218-4781-7 |page=xviii |edition=First |language=en}}</ref> It received positive reviews and is the textbook of choice for a number of universities.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Berg |first1=Michael |title=MAA Reviews Algebra: Chapter 0 |url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/algebra-chapter-0 |website=old.maa.org |publisher=Mathematical Association of America |access-date=4 August 2025 |date=17 September 2009 |archive-date=21 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250621155932/https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/algebra-chapter-0 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2021, Aluffi published another abstract algebra book aimed at undergraduate students, titled ''Algebra - Notes from the Underground''. What separates Aluffi's books from most abstract algebra texts is the ordering of the material. In ''Chapter 0'', Aluffi introduces [[category (mathematics)|categories]] and [[universal properties]] at the outset. In ''Notes from the Underground'', he takes a modern "[[Ring (mathematics)|ring]]-first" approach as opposed to the standard "[[Group (mathematics)|group]]-first" approach.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Aluffi |first1=Paolo |title=Algebra: Notes from the Underground |url=https://www.cambridge.org/us/universitypress/subjects/mathematics/algebra/algebra-notes-underground?format=PB |website=Cambridge University Press & Assessment |publisher=Cambridge University Press |access-date=16 August 2025 |language=en |date=2021 |archive-date=6 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240906191136/https://www.cambridge.org/us/universitypress/subjects/mathematics/algebra/algebra-notes-underground?format=PB |url-status=live }}</ref> The idea is that someone with no knowledge of [[abstract algebra]] will find it easier to learn about rings as they are already comfortable with the ring of integers.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Toller |first1=Owen |title=Algebra, notes from the underground by Paolo Aluffi |journal=The Mathematical Gazette |date=November 2023 |volume=107 |issue=570 |pages=562–563 |doi=10.1017/mag.2023.131 |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mathematical-gazette/article/algebra-notes-from-the-underground-by-paolo-aluffi-pp-488-2999-paper-isbn-9781108958233-cambridge-university-press-2021/75255C33843681F8CE8F1EF0B9748791 |publisher=Cambridge University Press|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Research==
Aluffi’s research is in [[algebraic geometry]]. Most of it deals with [[enumerative geometry]] and with
[[singularity theory]], specifically [[characteristic classes]] for singular varieties. He has also 
worked on questions in algebraic geometry motivated by connections with [[high energy physics]].
His collaborators include [[Carel Faber]], [[Matilde Marcolli]], and [[Jonathan Mboyo Esole]].<ref name="vita" >{{cite web |title=Paolo Aluffi |url=https://www.math.fsu.edu/~aluffi/ps+pdfs/NewCV.pdf |access-date=5 August 2025 |archive-date=17 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250217143651/https://www.math.fsu.edu/~aluffi/ps+pdfs/NewCV.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>
